picks.what: View from Petrovaradin Fortress across the Danube and the pontoon bridge, lithograph in Donau-Ansichten (Wien Museum)
picks.who: Jakob Alt and Adolph Friedrich Kunike
picks.why: general view of the town’s church towers beyond the pontoon bridge; margins, caption and fortress-wall foreground trimmed

picks.what: Aerial photograph of Petrovaradin Fortress, the bridge and Novi Sad (Historical City Archive Novi Sad)
picks.why: the city spread out across the Danube from the fortress; aircraft rigging at right trimmed

picks.file: Novi Sad, Petrovaradin, pohled z pevnosti.jpg
picks.what: View from Petrovaradin Fortress across the Danube to Novi Sad, photograph
picks.why: the classic view of the city and bridges from the fortress, over the old roofs of Petrovaradin; right half (Petrovaradin only) trimmed

gaps: P0–P2: no candidates. P4: only #5, a vaguely dated (‘beginning of the 19th century’) second version of the Alt view. P5 has only the low-resolution #6 besides the 1944 bombing photos.
notes: #6 is only 1024 px wide; Commons dates it 1920 and its bridge is the Potiorek Bridge (built 1915), so ‘about 1920’. #10’s Commons artist field holds only a notice text with no name; the CC BY 3.0 credit needs the uploader’s name from the file page. #11 (Bjoertvedt, 2012, hazy aerial of the whole city) is the alternative if a named author is required. #1/#4 show Sremska Kamenica, not Novi Sad; #3 is a crop of #2.
